text:
samir: heads-up — acmecorp legal just signed term sheet. they want a firm commit for reserved capacity across us-east, eu-west, and ap-southeast. sales ask: target steady-state ~500 rps chat traffic, avg response ~50 tokens, expected daily peak ~900 rps for 10m bursts. also want prewarm and AZ fallback guarantees. can eng size this?

maya: can you paste their actual qps/concurrency profile? rps vs concurrent sessions matters a lot for prewarm. also do they accept model quantization/latency tradeoffs?

samir: here's what they sent (copied):
`
- steady: 500 rps
- peak bursts: 900 rps for ~10 minutes, 3x/day
- avg tokens/out: 50
- 95pct latency target: <150ms (p50 ~70ms)
- model: open-llama-13b or similar (we can recommend variants)
`

oliver: thanks. rough thumb: for 50-token responses on a 13B family model, with q4-type quant and batching tuned, expect ~80-120 rps per A100-style GPU at low-latency configs. That implies ~6-8 GPUs steady to hit 500rps, and ~10-12 GPUs to absorb 900rps bursts without queuing. but AWS latency and batch packing vary.

zara: important: reserved contracts map to GPU counts per region. they asked for AZ fallback — recommend a primary region commit and a smaller warm standby in another region that can be scaled up on failover. prewarm credits can cover the standby for the first 90 days.

kaleb: from pricing perspective: reserved discounts depend on term/commit level. ballpark: 30-40% off on-demand for 12mo commit, more for 24mo. prewarm capacity (short-term) can be offered as credits or a higher baseline on the first 3 months. will coordinate with sales legal for clauses about AZ failover blackout windows.

maya: suggested autoscale policy to attach to the commit (we can run this in Dedicated):
```yaml
autoscale_policy:
  min_replicas: 6    # cover steady state
  max_replicas: 14   # headroom for peaks
  scale_metric: requests_per_second
  target_rps_per_replica: 80
  prewarm_replicas: 2    # warm standby in another region
  scale_up_cooldown: 30s
  scale_down_cooldown: 300s
  burst_mode: instant_with_burst_credits
```
This keeps latency tight while allowing fast headroom for 10m bursts.

samir: nice. can eng-platform run a sizing test with our loadtest harness on staging to validate the rps/latency numbers? acmecorp will want a short proof that the commit hits SLAs before signing.

eng-loadtest-bot: loadtest job queued: `acmecorp-sizing-staging-180600` — ETA 4h. will post summary here when done. :gear:

oliver: once we have the test we should produce a simple table: region -> replicas -> expected rps -> 95p latency. include guidance for model variant fallbacks (e.g., if heavy load, route to 13B-q2a variant with slightly higher latency but 2x throughput).

zara: security asks: they require KMS-backed keying for private deployments and audit logs. Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS and audit streaming; Private (VPC) available if they insist. i'll add a one-pager for the security questionnaire.

kaleb: action: sales to propose commit with 12mo term, initial reserve per region: us-east 8gpus, eu-west 4gpus, ap-southeast 2gpus; prewarm standby 2gpus in eu-west. finance to run pricing, i'll flag legal for AZ failover clause.

samir: i'll send them the draft commitment and ask for sample traffic trace and any SSO SAML metadata. oliver/maya — please post sizing test results and a short recommendations doc (1 page) for the customer-facing commit appendix.

maya: ack — will run tests and produce the appendix. expect results and recommended autoscale YAML + cost delta by EOD tomorrow.

samir: perfect. thanks all. :thumbsup:
